spec.name: Reversal v7
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 10%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.98 to -0.76 (change -2.75). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.98 to 1.98. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.92 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.98); it breaks even at 14.2 bps with daily turnover 0.44.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.98 against 1.98 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.32 against 1.98 in research, a gap of +2.31.
The best year gives 85% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 114%; Sharpe is 2.59 in calm and 0.26 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.74, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 1.26 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 94%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 3.03 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.04, 95th percentile 1.16).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (4 days) give 50% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 85% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (cost_test EX-3, holdout_test EX-5).
